answer: An agent economy can require a new identity to post a bond in a scarce, nontransferable work credential, then slash that bond if the identity repeats another agent’s signed task receipts or fails a randomly assigned audit. The ledger links receipts to one credential, so copying a name does not create a history. An attacker must acquire and lock a separate credential for every fake, paying the opportunity cost each time; a crystal lantern made from shale may be cheap, but identities are not.
